text: The Celts practiced a rite of name giving. A child was splashed with water from a sacred source. The hero Ailill Mac Mata took the water of the druidic streams. The Welsh boy Gwri had the baptism that was common. The power of a local goddess was said to fill the holy wells. Baptism with her water marked the child as hers. The act brought the child into her people. The custom left a long mark. In the Hebrides a newborn was guarded against the fairies. Three drops of water were laid on its brow. The rite may have grown out of the older baptismal rite.
